name: ValidatePortalAuth
description: Internal authentication helper used by every HC6 portal SP (and some others). Validates the caller's deviceId, looks up the device secret and owning hasher from HC.Device JOIN HC.Hasher, determines the caller type (regular user, HashRuns.org service account, admin portal service account) from PublicHasherId, builds the token param string, and validates the access token via HC6.CHECK_PORTAL_ACCESS_TOKEN. Regular devices: UPPER(DeviceSecret), with ':' + UPPER(callerParamString) appended when callerParamString is non-NULL. Service-account devices (empty DeviceSecret): UPPER(callerParamString) alone, no prefix. Returns hasherId and callerType through OUTPUT parameters; the caller checks @errorMessage. Returns no rowsets, writes nothing and logs nothing. NOT exposed as an API endpoint — called only by other HC6 SPs, which must pass OBJECT_NAME(@@PROCID) as @callerProcName.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: The caller's device ID. Looked up in HC.Device to retrieve the associated device secret and hasher. Required.

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Short-lived cryptographic token to validate via HC6.CHECK_PORTAL_ACCESS_TOKEN. No SQL default: callers always pass their own @accessToken (which may be NULL — a NULL token simply fails validation).

parameters.name: callerProcName
parameters.description: The calling SP's name. Caller MUST pass OBJECT_NAME(@@PROCID). Baked into the token hash on the Flutter client side — must match exactly for validation to succeed.

parameters.name: callerParamString
parameters.description: Optional context string baked into the token hash on the client side. Must match what Flutter passed to generateToken() as paramString. NULL when no extra context is used. For a regular device it is appended as ':' + UPPER(value) after UPPER(deviceSecret); for a service account (empty DeviceSecret) it is the whole param string.

parameters.name: errorMessage
parameters.description: OUTPUT (no default — must be supplied): set to NULL on success, 'deviceId is required' or 'Authentication failed' on failure.

parameters.name: hasherId
parameters.description: OUTPUT (no default — must be supplied): HC.Hasher.id (internal PK) of the device's user. NULL on failure.

parameters.name: callerType
parameters.description: OUTPUT (no default — must be supplied): 0=regular user, 1=HashRuns.org service account (PublicHasherId 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111), 2=admin portal service account (PublicHasherId 22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222). NULL when the device is unknown.

prerequisites: HC6.CHECK_PORTAL_ACCESS_TOKEN scalar function must exist (uses @deviceId instead of @publicHasherId, compared to HC.CHECK_PORTAL_ACCESS_TOKEN)
Service account rows must be pre-seeded in HC.Device for the hashers whose PublicHasherId is 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111 and 22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222
breakingChangeRules: Never change the OUTPUT parameter semantics
Never change callerType integer codes without updating all callers
Never change the token param string format (UPPER(deviceSecret) + callerParamString) without coordinating with Flutter

codeSmells.detail: @deviceId, @accessToken and @callerProcName (lines 2-4) and the three OUTPUT parameters (lines 6-8) have no SQL default. Harmless in practice: the helper is only called from other SPs, which always pass all of them; it is never an API endpoint.

The body (lines 51-122) has no TRY/CATCH and logs nothing. Callers deliberately invoke it OUTSIDE their own TRY block, so a runtime error here (e.g. inside HC6.CHECK_PORTAL_ACCESS_TOKEN) would surface as an unlogged 500. Low likelihood: two single-row lookups and a scalar function call.
